findings: components[1].sound_limitation: The limitation says the Baxter–Sagart table could not be inspected, but the dossier includes local primary readings for both 示 and 視 in that same system: 示 *s-gijʔ-s and 視 *gijʔ-s (also reflected in X-26e6ed1f8344248e7806). Keep the Mandarin comparison and phonetic-role caveat, but replace the claim that no usable historical comparison was inspected with the actual same-system pair and note that it differs by the reconstructed *s- prefix; the reconstruction supports compatibility, not proof of the graph’s phonetic role.

learner.overview: The traditional construction is described only as “見 for seeing and 示 for sound,” which is too compressed for a first-reading explanation. State plainly that 見 contributes the seeing-related meaning and 示 is the sound element, while keeping the eye-above-standing-figure interpretation qualified as proposed; cite the existing evidence IDs.

historical_glyphs.items[0].caption: The caption presents the oracle-style drawing as an early form of 視 without making clear in the caption that this is a proposed scholarly identification and a modern redraw. Revise it to call the pictured form a modern redraw of a proposed early graph interpreted as 視, and preserve the qualified eye-and-standing-figure interpretation, citing the existing evidence IDs.
